subject.title: feat(android): durable offline command outbox for chat sends

question: Should Android text-only offline commands ship as app-private Room rows with destructive schema-bump semantics after the correctness fixes and real-device proof, or should this wait for a stronger privacy/upgrade design?
rationale: The PR persists user-authored commands before they reach the Gateway and intentionally treats the shared chat database as destructively migratable; automation cannot choose that product/security boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Fix, prove, then sign off
options.body: Keep the PR open, fix the delivery bugs and i18n drift, add redacted Android real-behavior proof, then require explicit maintainer acceptance of storage, retention, and upgrade behavior before merge.

options.title: Narrow the storage scope
options.body: Reduce the feature to a nonpersistent or foreground-only queue if durable private command storage is not ready for this release path.

options.title: Accept the current storage model
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept app-private text-only storage and destructive migration, but that acceptance should be visible before merge.

recommendation.title: Fix, prove, then sign off
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, fix the delivery bugs and i18n drift, add redacted Android real-behavior proof, then require explicit maintainer acceptance of storage, retention, and upgrade behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The same person is the strongest current-history owner for Android chat/gateway code and authored the stacked Android outbox work.
